title: Add operator constraint enforcer and audit-federation shim for KMS residency annotations
author: Maya Patel
description: Context: Customers and internal audits require stronger operator boundaries and a way to prove KMS residency decisions end-to-end across regions. This PR introduces two coordinated pieces: 1) an RBAC v2 "operator constraint enforcer" that evaluates operator-scoped claims against a set of parameterized constraint templates (OPA), and 2) an "audit-federation" shim for the audit-forwarder that canonicalizes residency annotations, emits a federated audit stamp, and pseudonymizes operator identifiers for cross-region telemetry. Motivation: previous approaches relied on coarse deny-lists and ad-hoc middleware which made policy drift and cross-region reconciliation difficult. The enforcer provides a declarative, testable policy layer and the federation shim guarantees audit artifacts carry canonical residency proof (region, KMS provider, wrapped key id) while minimizing PII exposure. Summary of changes: - New package pkg/authz/enforcer implementing the RBAC v2 constraint evaluator that plugs into the policy decision flow. Supports per-operator TTL, action-scoped constraints, and a fast decision cache. - Rego templates under policies/opa/operator_constraints.rego with unit tests and example constraints for common operator roles. - Migration script scripts/migrate-operator-bindings.sh to translate a subset of existing operator bindings into constraint templates and to stage them under policies/managed/ - Audit-forwarder changes under pkg/audit/federation/ to add a federated audit-stamp header (X-RW-FED-AUDIT) and to route residency proofs to the residency-evidence store. Includes optional pseudonymization hooks configurable via values.yaml. - Helm and installer changes to expose toggles (deploy/helm/redwood-private/values.yaml) and a canary rollout plan (docs/security/operator-constraints.md). - Integration tests test/integration/policy_residency_test.go and CI policy-lint check to validate Rego and ensure no regressions. Backwards compatibility and rollout: feature guarded behind a runtime flag enforcer.enabled=false by default. The audit-federation shim is enabled in private deployments via values.yaml and can be toggled independently. Migration is provided as a best-effort script; operators will be staged in shadow mode before enforcement. Related linear items: ENG-3421 (operator constraints), ENG-3589 (audit federation), and a follow-up for metrics collection (ENG-3660). Checklist: - [x] OPA templates and unit tests - [x] Enforcer implementation and decision cache - [x] Audit stamp + pseudonymization config - [x] Migration script and docs - [x] Integration tests and CI policy-lint - [x] Docs and rollout notes Rolling forward: plan to enable shadow mode for a week in staging then opt-in small customers, with a two-week canary before org-wide enforcement.

release_notes: Adds RBAC v2 operator constraint enforcer with OPA templates, a federated audit shim that annotates KMS residency proofs and pseudonymizes operator identifiers; includes migration helpers and rollout guidance. Feature is disabled by default and can be enabled per-deployment.
notes_for_oncall: If operators see unexpected denies after enabling the enforcer, toggle enforcer.enabled=false to revert to previous behavior. Audit-federation can be disabled independently. Watch residency-evidence-store queue length and audit-forwarder error rate metrics.
